quizzes.title: Mokha Capture and Red Sea Stakes (MCQ)
quizzes.passage:
Yemen is experiencing a renewed round of fighting, and one recent development has drawn wide attention across the region. The Houthis, an Iran-aligned armed group in Yemen, have captured the strategic port town of Mocha, also written as Mokha, on the Red Sea coast. The capture expands Houthi control along Yemen's western coastline and marks a significant development in the country's conflict.

The event also affects Yemen's civil war more broadly. Strategically, Houthi control of Mocha strengthens the group's position in the area and could increase its leverage over regional maritime traffic. The Houthis emerged as an opposition movement during the 2000s, and they are also part of the Iranian-led Axis of Resistance. They are opposed to Israel and the United States.

The movement's current leader is Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, and the capital, Sanaa, is currently under Houthi control. The government that the Houthis oppose is internationally recognised, and its president is Rashad al-Alimi. The group's control of the port also fits into the wider pattern of Houthi expansion in western Yemen.

The development has implications that go beyond Yemen. Tensions involving Yemen, Saudi Arabia, Iran and other regional powers may intensify, and the events could affect global trade, energy security and Red Sea maritime security.

questions.q: In which Yemeni governorate is the port city of Mokha located?
questions.explanation: The booklet places Mokha in Taiz Governorate.

questions.q: Along with Mokha, the Houthis also seized which two islands?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Houthis seized Perim and Zuqar Islands along with Mokha.

questions.q: After Mokha fell, government forces moved south towards which coastal area?
questions.explanation: The booklet says government forces moved south towards Dhubab, a coastal area closer to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

questions.q:
Examine the two statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Mokha is important mainly for geopolitical and maritime reasons.
Reason (R): Its location enables the Houthis to threaten shipping routes linking the Indian Ocean, Red Sea and Suez Canal.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, and the threat to shipping routes is the reason the location gives Mokha its importance.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Hanish Islands   ->   A. Links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden
II. Bab el-Mandeb Strait   ->   B. Shut by Saudi Arabia after drone strikes from Iraq
III. East-West Oil Pipeline   ->   C. Houthi forces advanced towards them in the Red Sea
IV. Earlier Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping   ->   D. Forced some vessels onto longer routes around Africa
questions.explanation: Hanish Islands match C, Bab el-Mandeb Strait matches A, the East-West Oil Pipeline matches B, and the earlier attacks match D.

questions.q:
Examine the statements given below:
I. Government forces moved north towards Saada after Mokha fell.
II. Renewed fighting has caused civilian displacement.
III. Mokha lies about 80 km from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because government forces moved south, while II and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Mokha capture are correct?
I. The capture could affect the movement of oil and commodities between Asia and Europe.
II. The capture reduced Houthi control along Yemen's western coastline.
III. Government-aligned forces have lost an important coastal position.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is contrary to its statement that the capture expanded Houthi control.

quizzes.title: Mokha Capture and Red Sea Stakes (TITA)
quizzes.passage:
Yemen's renewed conflict has taken a new turn after the Houthis captured the strategic port city of Mocha, also written as Mokha, on the Red Sea coast. The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed group in Yemen. Their control now extends further along the western coastline, and government-aligned forces have lost an important coastal position. Mocha is described as a significant development in the renewed conflict.

The Houthis are described as an opposition movement that emerged during the 2000s. Their ideology centres on opposition to Israel and the United States, and they are part of the Iranian-led Axis of Resistance. Their current leader is Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, and the capital, Sanaa, is currently under Houthi control.

Mocha's location could increase the group's leverage over regional maritime traffic. Oil, commodities and other goods moving between Asia and Europe could be affected by the developments. Global trade, energy security and Red Sea maritime security are all involved in the outcome, while the civil war in Yemen continues. The internationally recognised president, Rashad al-Alimi, leads a government that now faces these new pressures, and its prime minister is Shaea al-Zindani. The recognised government controls only limited areas in the north, and rising jihadist threats from Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula have added to the country's security concerns.

questions.q: How far, in km, is Mokha from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait? (number)

quizzes.title: Yemen's North-South Divide (MCQ)
quizzes.passage:
Yemen has long been divided between its north and south. The two regions have distinct religious traditions, social structures and systems of governance, and these differences were reinforced by foreign influence and colonial legacies, particularly in the south. The divide is a long-standing feature of Yemen's politics.

The Cold War era also left a lasting mark, because each part of the country was shaped by outside powers during that period. Many of the divisions that exist today can be traced back to the way the two regions developed.

Southern discontent has surfaced repeatedly in the years since. The Southern Movement, known as Al-Hirak, continues to demand greater autonomy or independence for southern Yemen, and the south remains an important part of the country's internal divisions.

A separate council in the south, the Southern Transitional Council, also seeks autonomy or independence. Recent developments show that southern politics is linked with regional powers, which back different groups in the south. Yemen's internal divisions therefore remain relevant to understanding the country today. Yemen's north and south developed separate governance systems, and the booklet links these differences to the country's modern politics. This is why the divide is still discussed in the booklet's account of Yemen's internal divisions.

questions.q: Before the 1990 unification, which power backed South Yemen?
questions.explanation: The booklet states South Yemen was backed by the Soviet Union.

questions.q: In which year did North and South Yemen merge to form the Republic of Yemen?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the two states merged in 1990.

questions.q: In which year did southern leaders attempt secession, leading to a brief civil conflict?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the attempted secession and brief civil conflict to 1994.

questions.q:
Examine the two statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Yemen was a single country until 1990.
Reason (R): North Yemen was supported by the United States and Saudi Arabia.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says Yemen existed as two countries until 1990, so A is false, while R is stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Ali Abdullah Saleh   ->   A. Expanded influence in Hadramout and Mahra
II. Southern Movement (Al-Hirak)   ->   B. Governed North Yemen since 1978
III. Southern Transitional Council   ->   C. Formed in 2007
IV. Pro-government military bloc   ->   D. Receives backing from Saudi Arabia
questions.explanation: Saleh governed North Yemen since 1978, the Southern Movement formed in 2007, the STC expanded in Hadramout and Mahra, and the pro-government bloc receives Saudi backing.

questions.q:
Examine the statements given below:
I. The Southern Movement was formed in 1994.
II. The pro-government military bloc opposes the STC's separatist agenda.
III. Centralised power after unification created resentment in the south.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the Southern Movement was formed in 2007, while II and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the north-south divide are correct?
I. Ali Abdullah Saleh became President of the unified state.
II. The UAE backs the Southern Transitional Council.
III. The Southern Movement was formed in 1990.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the Southern Movement formed in 2007.

quizzes.title: Yemen's North-South Divide (TITA)
quizzes.passage:
Yemen has long been divided between its north and south. The two regions have distinct religious traditions, social structures and systems of governance, and these differences were reinforced by foreign influence and colonial legacies, especially in the south. The Cold War era added another layer, as both regions were tied to outside powers.

Southern discontent has resurfaced repeatedly. A movement continues to demand greater autonomy or independence for southern Yemen, and a separatist council in the south has expanded its influence in parts of the region. The Southern Transitional Council, which seeks autonomy or independence, has recently expanded its influence in Hadramout and Mahra. Opposing that council is a pro-government military bloc, which is closely aligned with the Hadramout tribal alliance and opposes the council separatist agenda.

Yemen's internal divisions therefore remain part of its political landscape. Its north and south have different histories, and the country's politics continues to reflect those differences in the present day, with several groups competing for influence across the region. Southern discontent and present-day politics cannot be separated from the north-south divide that shaped the country's past. The divisions also influence which outside powers each group receives support from. The council expansion has been noted in recent developments.

questions.q: Which country backed South Yemen before the 1990 unification? (name the country)
questions.explanation: The booklet states South Yemen was backed by the Soviet Union.

questions.q: In which year did North and South Yemen merge? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the two states merged in 1990 to form the Republic of Yemen.

questions.q: In which year did southern leaders attempt secession, leading to a brief civil conflict? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the attempted secession to 1994.

questions.q: In which year was the Southern Movement (Al-Hirak) formed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Southern Movement formed in 2007.

questions.q: In which year did Ali Abdullah Saleh begin governing North Yemen? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Saleh had governed North Yemen since 1978.

questions.q: Which Gulf state backs the Southern Transitional Council? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Southern Transitional Council as backed by the UAE.

questions.q: Which Gulf state gives political and strategic backing to the pro-government military bloc in the south? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pro-government military bloc receives political and strategic backing from Saudi Arabia.

quizzes.title: Mukalla Strike and UAE Withdrawal (MCQ)
quizzes.passage:
Yemen's south has been at the centre of recent political developments. A council in the south, the Southern Transitional Council, seeks autonomy or independence for southern Yemen and has recently expanded its influence in the Hadramout and Mahra areas. The council receives backing from the UAE.

Opposing the council is a pro-government military bloc. The bloc is closely aligned with the Hadramout tribal alliance, opposes the council's separatist agenda and receives political and strategic backing from Saudi Arabia. The two Gulf countries have therefore supported different sides in the south, and that backing has placed different groups in the south on opposite sides.

Tensions between them became visible in a recent incident at a port in southern Yemen. The UAE rejected the allegation linked to that incident. At the request of the Republic of Yemen, Saudi Arabia had earlier called on the UAE to withdraw its military elements from Yemeni territory within 24 hours and to refrain from providing any military or financial support to any party in the country.

The episode has drawn attention to the wider role of outside powers in Yemen's politics, and to how the internal divisions of the country are being shaped by the positions of regional states.

questions.q: Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on which port in southern Yemen?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the airstrikes as being on Mukalla Port.

questions.q: The shipment that reached the port before the strike came from which place?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the consignment came from Fujairah in the UAE.

questions.q: According to the UAE, what did the shipment consist of?
options: Vehicles meant exclusively for UAE forces
questions.explanation: The UAE said the shipment consisted of vehicles meant exclusively for its own forces.

questions.q:
Examine the two statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The UAE withdrew its troops from Yemen.
Reason (R): Escalating airstrikes raised security risks for UAE personnel in the region.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists security concerns among the reasons cited for the UAE troop withdrawal.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Mukalla Port   ->   A. Confined to counter-terrorism operations
II. Fujairah   ->   B. Port in the UAE where the consignment originated
III. Riyadh's allegation   ->   C. Alleged arms transfer to separatist groups
IV. UAE military presence in Yemen   ->   D. Struck by Saudi airstrikes
questions.explanation: Mukalla was struck by Saudi airstrikes, Fujairah is the port of origin, Riyadh alleged an arms transfer, and the UAE presence is limited to counter-terrorism.

questions.q:
Examine the statements given below:
I. The UAE said the consignment carried vehicles meant for its own forces.
II. The UAE termed Saudi allegations of an arms transfer accurate.
III. The UAE's military presence in Yemen is confined to counter-terrorism operations.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the UAE called the claims unfounded, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Mukalla incident are correct?
I. The UAE said Yemen's future should be decided by Yemenis themselves.
II. Escalating airstrikes raised risks to UAE personnel in the region.
III. The UAE accepted that the vehicles were meant for separatist groups.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the UAE denied any arms transfer to separatists.

quizzes.title: Mukalla Strike and UAE Withdrawal (TITA)
quizzes.passage:
Southern Yemen has been at the centre of recent political and military developments. Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on a port in the south after a shipment arrived there from a neighbouring Gulf state. Saudi officials alleged the shipment contained arms for separatist groups.

The state that sent the shipment rejected the allegation, saying the cargo was meant for its own forces and that the claims were unfounded. It has also said its military presence in Yemen is limited to counter-terrorism operations. At the request of the Republic of Yemen, Saudi Arabia had earlier asked that state to withdraw its military elements within 24 hours. The state has said that Yemen's future political structure should be determined by Yemenis themselves.

A council in the south seeks autonomy or independence, and it has recently expanded its influence in the region. Opposing it is a pro-government military bloc that receives backing from Saudi Arabia, and the two Gulf states have supported different sides in the south. The council separatist agenda and its foreign backing remain at the centre of the debate about the south, and escalating airstrikes raised risks for personnel in the region. The episode is one of several recent developments in the south.

questions.q: Which port in southern Yemen was struck by Saudi airstrikes? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the airstrikes as being on Mukalla Port in southern Yemen.

questions.q: Which UAE port city did the consignment come from? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the consignment came from Fujairah in the UAE.

questions.q: Which city's government alleged that the shipment contained arms for separatists? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Riyadh alleged the consignment contained arms for southern separatist groups.

questions.q: What did the sending state say the shipment consisted of? (one word)
questions.explanation: The UAE said the shipment consisted of vehicles meant exclusively for its own forces.

questions.q: Which council in the south seeks autonomy or independence? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Southern Transitional Council seeks autonomy or independence for Southern Yemen.

questions.q: The council has recently expanded its influence into Mahra and which other area? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Southern Transitional Council has recently expanded its influence in Hadramout and Mahra.

questions.q: Which country says its military presence in Yemen is limited to counter-terrorism operations? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE's military presence in Yemen is confined to counter-terrorism operations.
